memory.content: The author card typically shows a description and a social QR image; on mobile it was refined with centered QR codes and a separator.

Comments are an optional per-site capability: 'some site may not config the comment section, and some posts may not config ExternalLinks'. Page sections must render correctly when a site disables comments or a post lacks external links; site-wide provider config may be null and page-level settings layer on top.

The maintainer keeps npm dependencies minimal: when a change added four new packages he questioned each one ('does we realy need these four packages?') and accepted them only after a per-package justification. New capabilities should first try existing dependencies or a small in-house implementation; a recommended npm package is adopted only when the team accepts the added weight.
The feed defaults decided on March 2: full-text content by default ('I think full can be default'), with configurable format (rss/atom/both) and maxItems in site config.

Feed freshness is checked in a real RSS reader after a build and deploy, not by inspecting XML alone. In early March a reader subscription showed new posts missing after a deploy even though the generated XML looked fine, because the feed is produced at build time; the practice is to build, serve or deploy `out/`, then subscribe and confirm the new items appear.
Single-language sites can disable i18n entirely via siteConfig.i18n.enabled=false; the language switcher hides and localStorage reads/writes are skipped. The shipped demo site stays bilingual.

Non-blocking environment or tooling defects found during sessions are recorded as GitHub issues so they persist across sessions, instead of only being noted in the conversation. Established March 5 when the maintainer asked to 'post an issue about this remaining issues' after the feed/graph session.

The JSON-LD structured data (March 5) maps schema types per content type - BlogPosting for posts, Article for book chapters, Book for books - and BreadcrumbList was evaluated and dropped as low value.

# Plan: create-amytis CLI (Model A)

## Context

Users want to start a new Amytis-based site without forking/cloning the repo manually.
The CLI (`bunx create-amytis my-blog`) will scaffold a full Amytis project by downloading
the latest GitHub release tarball, then asking two setup questions (site title, description)
before patching `site.config.ts` and running `bun install`.

Model A: user gets the full source — `src/`, `scripts/`, `content/`, `site.config.ts`.
They own all the code; only `content/` and `site.config.ts` need to be touched day-to-day.

---

## Package structure

```
packages/
  create-amytis/
    package.json      ← name: "create-amytis", bin: "dist/index.js"
    src/
      index.ts        ← CLI entry point
    dist/             ← compiled output (gitignored, published to npm)
    tsconfig.json
    .gitignore
```

Root `package.json` gets a bun workspace entry:
```json
"workspaces": ["packages/*"]
```

---

## CLI flow

```
bunx create-amytis [project-name]
```

1. Read `project-name` from `process.argv[2]`; if missing, prompt for it
2. Call GitHub API to get latest release tag:
   `GET https://api.github.com/repos/hutusi/amytis/releases/latest`
3. Download tarball:
   `https://github.com/hutusi/amytis/archive/refs/tags/{tag}.tar.gz`
4. Extract into `./{project-name}/`  (tarball root dir is `amytis-{version}/`, rename it)
5. Prompt for **Site title** (default: project-name)
6. Prompt for **Site description** (default: "My digital garden")
7. Patch `site.config.ts`:
   - Replace `title: { en: "Amytis", zh: "Amytis" }` with user title
   - Replace `description: { en: "...", zh: "..." }` with user description
8. Patch `package.json` in scaffolded dir:
   - Set `"name"` to project-name
   - Set `"private": true` (they're not publishing this)
   - Remove `"repository"`, `"bugs"`, `"homepage"` fields
9. Run `bun install` in the new directory
10. Print success + next steps

---

## Critical files to create

### `packages/create-amytis/package.json`
```json
{
  "name": "create-amytis",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Create a new Amytis digital garden",

  "bin": { "create-amytis": "./dist/index.js" },
  "scripts": {
    "build": "bun build src/index.ts --outfile dist/index.js --target node --sourcemap=none",
    "dev": "bun src/index.ts"
  },
  "files": ["dist"]
}
```

memory.content: Relative image paths (e.g. images/digital-garden.svg next to a content file) are supported and must work for every content type - posts, books, flows, series, custom pages - and any future content type.
The social label for the former Twitter account is displayed as 'X (Twitter)' or 'X/Twitter'; plain 'Twitter' or 'Twitter/X' are not used in the footer.

During the March 5 shared-utilities refactor the maintainer set a standing UI rule: eliminate component redundancy and ensure all components share some consistent style. Sections listing the same kind of content (latest writing, flows, series, books) use the same header/link patterns and title sizing; inconsistencies get aligned, not given one-off treatments.
With output: export, generateStaticParams must enumerate redirect targets so redirectFrom routes are generated at build time.

Post URLs are the permanent SEO identity and must remain stable when collections or series views are introduced. Collections reuse existing series/post URL patterns and must never change an already-published post URL; extra collection context is carried by a query parameter, not a new path.

skills.name: build-triage
skills.description: Triage a failing bun build/validate in this repo by error class and apply the minimal fix.
skills.content:
# Build triage

## Purpose
Diagnose and minimally fix failing builds in this repo.

## Use when
- A build or validate command fails.

## Do not use when
- Runtime browser issues; content typo fixes.

## Inputs
- The failing command and its error output.

## Procedure
1. Reproduce with the exact failing command (`bun run build`, `bun run build:dev`, or `bun run validate`) and read the first error, not the tail.
2. Classify the error class: module resolve errors are dependency/config issues; TypeScript type errors point at source types; a missing param in generateStaticParams means every routable URL must be enumerated under output: export; CSS resolve errors point at globals.css imports.
3. Apply the minimal fix without adding dependencies, then re-run the failing command and `bun run validate` until green.

## Verification
- bun run validate passes end to end.

## Constraints
- Do not add dependencies to silence build errors without asking.

skills.name: feed-standards
skills.description: Standards checklist for changing this repo's RSS/Atom feed outputs: content types, output sync, and verification.
skills.content:
# Feed standards

## Purpose
Keep this repo's RSS/Atom HTTP content types and generated outputs aligned.

## Use when
- Choosing or changing feed Content-Type headers, or applying a feed-generation change that must be mirrored across RSS and Atom.

## Do not use when
- Deciding how to smoke-test a deploy in a real RSS reader (that is a separate historical practice).
- HTML meta/link tag changes; sitemap changes; adding a third-party feed library.

## Inputs
- The feed route handlers (`feed.xml`, `feed.atom`) and site config baseUrl.

## Procedure
1. Check per-route content types: the RSS route (`feed.xml`) must serve Content-Type `application/rss+xml` (not generic `application/xml`) and the Atom route (`feed.atom`) `application/atom+xml`.
2. Mirror the change across RSS and Atom outputs so both stay in sync; do not update only one format.
3. Parse both generated XML files and confirm they carry the same item set (same entries, same order).

## Verification
- HTTP Content-Type headers match the IANA types above, and both outputs parse as XML with identical item sets.

## Constraints
- Do not drop one output format in favor of the other without asking.

skills.name: image-perf-audit
skills.description: Audit page-weight/image performance for this static site: WebP coverage, eager/lazy split, heavy-library loading.
skills.content:
# Image performance audit

## Purpose
Audit and fix page-weight issues in this static site.

## Use when
- A performance review of images or first-load weight is requested.

## Do not use when
- Backend/API performance; build-time optimizations unrelated to page weight.

## Inputs
- The page/component tree and next.config image settings.

## Procedure
1. Check ExportedImage/WebP coverage: every local image must render through ExportedImage so next-image-export-optimizer emits WebP at build; bypassing it previously shipped original formats.
2. Check the eager/lazy split: above-the-fold cover images load eagerly; everything else loads lazily.
3. Check conditional loading of heavy client libraries (mermaid, katex) so they load only on pages that use them.
4. Verify with `bun run build:dev` plus the browser network panel.

## Verification
- No original-format local images ship in out/; LCP image loads eagerly.

## Constraints
- Do not degrade visual quality without asking.

skills.name: obsidian-import
skills.description: Import an Obsidian vault's journals and notes into this repo as flows and notes.
skills.content:
# Obsidian import

## Purpose
Import Obsidian journals/notes as flows/notes.

## Use when
- The user asks to bring Obsidian content into the site.

## Do not use when
- Hand-writing new content; importing from PDF or images.

## Inputs
- The Obsidian vault directory.

## Procedure
1. Point the importer at the vault directory as a CLI argument; journals map to flows and notes to notes.
2. Normalize filenames to URL-style slugs (lowercase, hyphens, symbols removed) and rewrite wiki-links to match.
3. Leave imported files uncommitted: never stage or commit imported content automatically.

## Verification
- Imported files build and resolve wiki-links.

## Constraints
- Never auto-commit imported content.

skills.name: pagefind-index
skills.description: Regenerate and sanity-check the Pagefind search index used by this site.
skills.content:
# Pagefind index

## Purpose
Regenerate the build-time search index.

## Use when
- Search results are stale after content changes.

## Do not use when
- Changing the search UI.

## Inputs
- A built out/ directory.

## Procedure
1. The index is generated by pagefind at build time; run `bun run build:dev` to regenerate public/pagefind. `bun dev` alone does not refresh it.
2. Open the search modal and query for newly added content to confirm the index includes it.

## Verification
- The search modal finds newly added content.

## Constraints
- The index only updates at build time; bun dev alone does not refresh it.

skills.name: selective-commit
skills.description: Commit completed work in this repo with selective staging, validation first, and conventional-commit subjects.
skills.content:
# Selective commit

## Purpose
Commit completed task work with selective staging, validation, and repo-conventional messages.

## Use when
- The user asks to commit the current task's changes, optionally including named extra files.
- The user asks to amend the previous commit.

## Do not use when
- The user only wants a diff review or code changes without a commit.
- Bulk history rewrites or branch management.

## Inputs
- Working tree state (git status/diff), the user's instruction naming any extra files.

## Procedure
1. Map changed files to the current task; stage exactly those files plus extras the user named. Never sweep in unrelated files, test-results/, or playwright-report/ (gitignored).
2. Run `bun run validate` (lint + tests + build:dev) and make it pass before committing.
3. Compose a conventional-commit subject matching repo history (feat/fix/docs/chore, `!` for breaking default changes). Amend an existing commit only when the user explicitly asks.
4. Commit and report the resulting hash and what was staged.

## Verification
- git status is clean afterwards except intentionally unstaged local-only changes.
- The commit subject matches repo history style.

## Constraints
- Never commit gitignored artifacts (test-results/, playwright-report/).
- Do not force-push or rewrite history beyond the requested amend.

skills.name: test-updates
skills.description: Decide and implement test updates for a change in this repo: layer mapping, breadth, and the suite commands to run.
skills.content:
# Test updates

## Purpose
Keep this repo's tests aligned with a change: right layers, right breadth, right commands.

## Use when
- A behavior change, bug fix, or new feature needs tests added or updated.

## Do not use when
- Debugging an unrelated failing environment; benchmarking.

## Inputs
- The diff or change description; the existing tests/ layout.

## Procedure
1. Classify the change by layer and pick test locations: src/lib helpers to tests/unit or co-located tests, content/routing pipeline to tests/integration, UI behavior to tests/e2e (mobile UI to tests/e2e/mobile), scripts to tests/tooling.
2. Decide breadth: user-visible behavior gets integration AND e2e coverage (the March 5 refactor episode asked for both).
3. Implement the tests so they fail for the right reason before the fix, then run `bun test` (src, tests/unit, tests/tooling, packages/create-amytis) plus `bun run test:int`, and `bun run test:e2e` for UI changes, until the full set passes.

## Verification
- bun test and bun run test:int (and test:e2e for UI) all pass.
- New tests fail for the right reason before the fix and pass after.

## Constraints
- Do not weaken existing assertions to make suites pass.
- Keep per-case mocks isolated; do not let one test's mocks leak into another.
